canned.title: Refund policy
canned.body: Thanks for reaching out. Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase for unused items and within 14 days for opened ones. Once we receive the return scan from the carrier, the refund is issued automatically and lands on your card within 3-5 business days.

canned.title: Shipping delay
canned.body: Sorry about the wait on your order. Carrier tracking sometimes lags a day or two behind the actual movement of the package. I have asked the carrier for a trace and will update you here as soon as they respond.

canned.title: Password reset
canned.body: You can reset your password from the sign-in page via "Forgot password" — the email arrives within a minute or two. If it does not show up, check the spam folder and make sure the address matches the one on the account. Reply here if you are still locked out and I will reset it manually after an identity check.

canned.title: API rate limits
canned.body: The API allows 600 requests per minute per token, measured over a sliding window. Responses include X-RateLimit-Remaining so your client can back off before hitting a 429. For bulk work, batching into chunks of 50 with a short pause between them stays comfortably under the limit.

canned.title: Plan comparison
canned.body: Team is $12 per seat and covers shared inboxes, views and reporting. Business is $18 per seat and adds SSO, audit logs and priority support. Upgrades are prorated to the day, so you only pay the difference for the remainder of the current cycle.

canned.title: Closing thanks
canned.body: Glad that is sorted. I will close this ticket now, but replying to this email reopens it at any time — no need to start over. Thanks for your patience.

canned.title: Acknowledge + investigating
canned.body: Thanks for the detailed report — I can reproduce what you are seeing and I am digging into it now. I will follow up here as soon as I have something concrete, and sooner if I need anything else from you.

canned.title: Need more info
canned.body: Happy to help get to the bottom of this. Could you share the account email, roughly when it started, and a screenshot or the exact error text? That will let me pinpoint it much faster.

canned.title: Escalated to engineering
canned.body: I have escalated this to our engineering team with the details you provided and a link to your account. It is now tracked on their side; I will relay updates here as they come and let you know the moment it is fixed.

canned.title: Bug confirmed + workaround
canned.body: You have found a genuine bug — thank you. A fix is on the way; in the meantime, the workaround below should keep you moving. I will update this ticket when the fix ships so you can drop the workaround.

canned.title: Feature request logged
canned.body: Great suggestion — I have logged it with our product team and linked your account so we can follow up if it ships. I cannot promise a date, but demand from customers like you is exactly what moves these up the list.

canned.title: Duplicate charge refund
canned.body: I can see the duplicate charge and I am sorry for the scare. I have refunded the extra transaction; it will drop off your statement within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. The original, correct charge stays in place.

canned.title: Assign to me + working on it
canned.body: I have got this one — thanks for your patience. I am on it now and will keep you posted right here. No need to do anything on your end for the moment.

kb.title: Set up your first inbox view
kb.body: Views are saved filters over your tickets. Start with the built-in All, Unassigned, and My open views, then add your own by combining a status, a priority, and an assignee. Most small teams run one shared triage view plus a personal view per agent so nobody trips over each other.

kb.title: Keyboard shortcuts cheat sheet
kb.body: BaseDesk is keyboard-first. In the inbox, use j and k to move between tickets, Enter to open, e to solve, u to assign to yourself, and 1 to 4 to set priority. Inside a ticket, r focuses the reply box and n starts an internal note. Press ? anywhere to see the full list, or Ctrl/Cmd K to open the command palette.

kb.title: How refunds are processed
kb.body: Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase for unused items and within 14 days for opened ones. Once the return scan comes back from the carrier, the refund is issued automatically and lands on the original card within 3 to 5 business days. Duplicate charges are refunded as soon as we can see both on our side.

kb.title: Update your VAT or tax ID
kb.body: Add or correct a VAT or tax ID from the billing profile before an invoice is generated. If an invoice was already cut without the ID, we can reissue it with the correct details and, where VAT was charged in error, raise a credit note for the difference. Reissued invoices appear in your billing history.

kb.title: Handling rate limits (429s)
kb.body: The API allows 600 requests per minute per token, measured over a sliding window. Every response includes an X-RateLimit-Remaining header so your client can back off before hitting a 429. For bulk work, batch into chunks of about 50 requests with a short pause between them to stay comfortably under the limit.

kb.title: Reset two-factor authentication
kb.body: If you have lost your authenticator and your backup codes, reply from the billing email on the account and include the last four digits of the card on file. After an identity check we reset 2FA and add an entry to the audit log. Set up fresh backup codes right after you are back in so this does not recur.

kb.title: Invite your team and set roles
kb.body: Add teammates from Settings then Team. Admins manage billing, channels and other agents; agents work tickets. An invite email carries a one-time link that expires in seven days — resend it from the same screen if it lapses. You can change anyone’s role later without re-inviting them.

kb.title: Connect an email channel
kb.body: Forward your support address to the inbound address shown under Channels, or connect a mailbox directly. New mail lands as a ticket, replies thread back to the customer, and the original From name and address are preserved. Send a test message after connecting to confirm both directions work.

kb.title: Change your plan or seat count
kb.body: Upgrade, downgrade or adjust seats from the billing profile at any time. Increases are prorated to the day so you only pay the difference for the rest of the cycle; decreases take effect at the next renewal. Annual plans can add seats mid-term at the annual rate.

kb.title: Understand your invoice
kb.body: Each invoice lists the plan, the seat count for the period, any proration lines from mid-cycle changes, and tax where it applies. The billing history keeps every invoice as a PDF. If a charge looks wrong, reply with the invoice number and we will walk through the lines with you.

kb.title: Authenticate with API tokens
kb.body: Create a token under Settings then API and send it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Tokens carry the permissions of the agent who created them, so scope them to a service account for automations. Rotate a token by creating a new one and deleting the old; revocation is immediate.

kb.title: Verify inbound webhook signatures
kb.body: Every webhook we send includes a signature header computed as an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using your endpoint secret. Recompute it on your side and compare in constant time before trusting the payload. Reject anything that does not match, and keep a short replay window on the timestamp.

kb.title: Set up single sign-on (SSO)
kb.body: Business plans can require SSO for all agents. Point your identity provider at the SAML endpoint under Settings then Security, map email as the primary attribute, and test with one account before enforcing. Once enforced, password sign-in is disabled and access follows your directory.

kb.title: Export or delete your data
kb.body: Admins can export tickets and contacts to CSV from Settings then Data, and request a full account export. To remove a specific person’s data on request, delete the contact — their tickets are anonymised and attachments purged. Deletions are logged in the audit trail.

kb.title: Track a delayed order
kb.body: Carrier tracking often lags a day or two behind the parcel’s real movement, especially over weekends and holidays. If a label shows created but has not scanned in 48 hours, we open a trace with the carrier and keep you updated here. Most traced parcels surface within a few business days.

kb.title: Send tickets to Slack
kb.body: Add a Slack channel under Channels to post new tickets and replies into a workspace channel, or route a specific inbox there. Threading keeps each ticket in its own Slack thread, and agents can reply from BaseDesk without leaving the customer conversation. Outbound uses a signed webhook.

kb.title: Build a custom report
kb.body: Open Reports then New report to combine a metric (volume, solved, resolution time, or CSAT) with a dimension (day, agent, priority, status, category, or tag) over a time range. Save it to revisit later. The overview page already covers the common cuts, so start there before building your own.

kb.title: Route tickets with rules
kb.body: Automation rules run on create or on update: match on subject, body, priority, channel or sender, then set a priority, add a tag, assign an agent, change status or set a category. Rules run top to bottom, so order the specific ones first. Time-based rules handle escalations for tickets left waiting.

kb.title: Complete API reference
kb.body:
# API reference

The BaseDesk API is a JSON-over-HTTPS API. Every request is authenticated with a **Bearer token** scoped to the permissions of the agent who created it.

> **Base URL:** `https://api.basedesk.example/v1` — every path below is relative to it.

## Authentication

Send your token in the `Authorization` header on every request:

```bash
curl https://api.basedesk.example/v1/tickets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

Create tokens under **Settings → API**. Rotate one by creating a new token and deleting the old — revocation is immediate.

## Rate limits

Limits are per token, over a 60-second sliding window. Every response carries these headers:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Requests allowed per window |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix time the window resets |

Exceeding the limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Back off using `Reset` rather than retrying in a tight loop.

## Core endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/tickets` | List tickets, filtered by `status`, `assignee`, `tag` |
| `POST` | `/tickets` | Open a ticket |
| `GET` | `/tickets/:id` | One ticket with its messages |
| `POST` | `/tickets/:id/messages` | Reply or add a note |
| `PATCH` | `/tickets/:id` | Update status, priority, assignee or tags |

### Creating a ticket

Post the requester and an opening message:

```json
{
  "subject": "Charged twice for Pro",
  "requesterEmail": "sofia@example.com",
  "priority": "high",
  "body": "I see two charges within seconds of each other."
}
```

A successful create returns `201` with the new ticket and its `number`.

## Error codes

Errors return a JSON body with a machine `code` and a human `message`.

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid_request` | A field is missing or malformed |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| `404` | `not_found` | The resource does not exist |
| `409` | `conflict` | e.g. replying to a closed ticket |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | Too many requests |

## Webhooks

Subscribe to events to react in real time. Each delivery is signed:

1. Compute `HMAC-SHA256` of the raw body with your endpoint secret.
2. Compare it, in constant time, to the `X-BaseDesk-Signature` header.
3. Reject mismatches, and enforce a short timestamp window to block replays.

Events include `ticket.created`, `ticket.updated`, `message.created` and `ticket.reopened`.

---

Something missing? Reach us at [support@basedesk.example](mailto:support@basedesk.example).

kb.title: Onboarding runbook: signup to first resolved ticket
kb.body:
# Onboarding runbook

This takes a new workspace from **signup to first resolved ticket** in about 30 minutes. Work top to bottom — each step builds on the last.

## 1. Set up your team

Invite the people who will work tickets and give them a role.

| Role | Can do | Cannot do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Admin** | Everything — billing, channels, agents, settings | — |
| **Agent** | Work tickets, write KB, run reports | Manage billing or other agents |

Send invites from **Settings → Team**. Invites expire after 7 days.

## 2. Connect a channel

Tickets have to come from somewhere. The fastest path is email:

- Forward your support address (e.g. `help@yourco.com`) to the inbound address under **Channels**.
- Send a test message and confirm it lands as a ticket.
- Reply from BaseDesk and confirm the customer receives it.

> Chat, webhook, Slack and the rest work the same way — connect, test both directions, done.

## 3. Triage with views

Views are saved filters. Start with the built-ins:

1. **Unassigned** — the shared queue nobody owns yet.
2. **My open** — your personal workload.
3. **Awaiting reply** — the ball is in your court.

## 4. Reply faster

Two tools cut reply time the most:

- **Canned replies** — pre-written answers. Type `/` in the composer to insert one.
- **Macros** — a canned reply *plus* actions (status, tags, assignee) in one click.

## 5. Close the loop

Solve the ticket when the customer is happy. A customer reply reopens it automatically, so there is no risk in solving early.

---

That is the whole loop: **intake → triage → reply → solve**. Everything else just makes one of those four faster.

kb.title: Plans & pricing explained
kb.body:
# Plans & pricing

BaseDesk has two paid plans, billed **per active agent per month**. Change plans anytime — increases are prorated to the day.

## Compare plans

| Feature | Team — $12/seat | Business — $18/seat |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Shared inboxes & views | Yes | Yes |
| Canned replies & macros | Yes | Yes |
| Reporting | Core | Advanced |
| SSO / SAML | — | Yes |
| Audit log | — | Yes |
| Priority support | — | Yes |

## How proration works

Add a seat mid-cycle and you pay only the remaining days:

```
charge = seat_price × (days_left_in_cycle ÷ days_in_cycle)
```

Downgrades take effect at the **next** renewal, so you keep what you paid for until then.

## Invoices

Every invoice lists:

- The plan and the seat count for the period
- Any proration lines from mid-cycle changes
- Tax, where it applies

Find them under **Settings → Billing → History** as downloadable PDFs.

> Spot a charge that looks wrong? Reply with the invoice number and we will walk through it line by line.
